subject: Post-call: Solstice Health — fit summary & proposed next step
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tang <alex.tang@solsticehealth.com>, Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@solsticehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T15:22:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Solstice Health — fit summary & proposed next step

Hi Alex / Emma,

Thanks again for taking 30 minutes today — appreciated the context on your ingestion pipeline and the 3 use cases you outlined (note classification at ingest, interactive discovery for care teams, and nightly batch embeddings for analytics). Quick recap and proposed next step below.

Recap (what I heard)
- Ingest: 100k docs/day, mostly PDFs and scanned forms; latency requirement for interactive queries ~200–300ms P95.
- Discovery for care teams: short multi-turn conversations, session affinity important to keep KV cache warm.
- Analytics embeddings: nightly job, cost sensitivity is high for bulk embedding runs.

Where Redwood can help (fit signals)
- Our private deployment supports on-prem/VPC for PHI (you flagged compliance as priority).
- Prefix/KV caching and continuous batching help keep interactive latency in your target SLO.
- Our Optimize recommendations can reduce embedding unit cost for the nightly job.

Ask / proposed next step
- If this looks right, can we book a brief technical fit call with your infra lead (15–20m) next week to validate network/KMS constraints and run a sample inference? I can bring one of our infra engineers.

Attachments: postcall-summary.pdf (summary + proposed mutual action plan), roi-estimate.xlsx (back-of-envelope cost comparison).

If you prefer, reply with a quick note on whether this is a possible fit or not — any reply helps us prioritize.

Thanks,
Lauren
